newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian gays fear sex scandals will spark backlash.
newsitem.headline: Belgian gays fear sex scandals will spark backlash.

text.p: Belgian homosexuals fear a recent spate of child sex scandals that rocked the country will spark a conservative backlash against them.

"What we are witnessing now is that all forms of sex which are not directly aimed at procreation are associated with abnormality," Anke Hintjens, spokeswoman for the Federation of Homosexual Workgroups, told Reuters on Wednesday.

As she spoke, a parliamentary commission was looking into a report by the Brussels prosecutor-general which according to the media alleges deputy prime minister Elio Di Rupo, 45, had sex with under-age boys.
Di Rupo has strongly denied the allegations.
The commission must decide whether or not to lift Di Rupo's constitutional immunity and refer him to the country's highest court, a move which would end his career.

The allegations have thrown Di Rupo's homosexuality in the spotlight in the worst possible way. His constituents were mostly unaware of his sexuality which was only known to an inner circle of politicians and journalists.
Di Rupo, the affable son of Italian immigrants and known for his bow-ties, had chosen to remain discreet about his sexuality.

"And that is how it should be," Olivier Deleuze, head of the ecologist parties' faction in parliament, told Reuters. "People do not need to know about the sexual preferences of their neighbour, pharmacist or mayor," he said.
"We are not all married men or women with children, and that is our right," Deleuze said in a speech to parliament on Tuesday.
But many gay rights activivists say that if Di Rupo had been more open about his homosexuality, the damage would not have been as great.

"Everyone is publicly known as a heterosexual unless one manifests oneself as homosexual. It is sad that apparently politicians cannot be open about their homosexuality," Yvan Brys, a spokesman for the Pink Action Front told Reuters.

The Front has started a debate about "outing" in Belgium, a form of political action by homosexuals in the United States which consists of publicly declaring the homosexuality of well known figures who have chosen to remain discreet.
"The court has done the outing for Di Rupo," he said.

Brys said that the gay liberation movement had already been dealt a severe blow by a (heterosexual) paedophile kidnap, sex and murder scandal of the past months, in which convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux is the main suspect.

He added that the Di Rupo affair would just make things worse and said legislative initiatives, such as a proposal to make discrimation of gays and lesbians illegal, had been blocked by the new climate of moral righteousness in Belgium.
Brys said there had been recent incidents of gay couples being thrown out of discos, apparently as a consequence of the Dutroux affair.
Ghent State University sociology professor John Vincke, who has published extensively on gay issues, said: "Our society is in a deep crisis and people are looking for a scapegoat."
